messages:
Maya R: FYI customer CS-9421 reports embeddings shape changed after we enabled an int8 quantization profile. They used to get 768-d vectors; now their downstream vector-store errors: "dimension mismatch: expected 768 got 384". Happened after a toggle yesterday.

Alex P: Can you paste the request_id + model name + exact curl they used? Also which SDK/lang.

Maya R: Request id req_0a1b2c3d, model= model-embed-ada (alias), quantization=int8. Using plain python requests. Their example curl:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"model-embed-ada","input":["test sentence"],"quantization":"int8","batch_size":16}'
```

They pasted the response snippet:

```json
{"object":"list","data":[{"object":"embedding","embedding":[0.001, -0.002, ...],"index":0,"length":384}]}
```

Alex P: Tagging Eng-ML — @Samir V can you take a look? @support-bot please pull traces for req_0a1b2c3d.

support-bot: Collected trace -> route=embeddings.create, node=embed-prod-12, req=req_0a1b2c3d, kernel=quantize-int8-v2, deploy=1845557600

Samir V: Quick theory notes — quantization should NOT change the output dimensionality. Two likely causes:
1) different model variant got routed (e.g., model-embed-ada-384 versus 768) due to alias resolution or routing rule when quantization param present.
2) client/SDK is misinterpreting a packed int8/binary payload as floats and ends up with a different perceived length.

Can you share raw response Content-Length / raw body (base64) if the customer captured it?

Maya R: They pasted raw body base64 (trimmed): "SGVsbG8...". Raw content-length header: 3072 bytes.

Samir V: Quick math: 3072 bytes aligns with 768 float32s (768 * 4 = 3072). If the response contains float32 array you'd expect length=768. If the customer sees length=384 but we have 3072 bytes that's suspicious. Possible that server served int8 (1 byte per entry) and client is decoding incorrectly — but that would produce content-length ~=384, not 3072. So mixed signals. Two hypotheses remain: (A) server emitted float32 for 768 dims and client truncated or collapsed pairs into single values somehow; (B) server actually routed to a 384-d model variant for the alias when quantization param was present.

Tanvi K: I dug into the recent deploys: there was a promoted variant model-embed-ada-384-int8 rolled earlier today to support super-low-cost embeddings for some customers. Deploy-bot shows promotion at 1845557600.

deploy-bot: promoted model-embed-ada-384-int8 -> production (deploy 1845557600) :rocket:

Alex P: If alias model-embed-ada resolves to a different variant depending on quantization flag, that's a bug — alias resolution must be orthogonal to quantization. Maya, can the customer try explicitly requesting model-embed-ada-768 (full name) and confirm shape?

Maya R: Customer tried explicit model name model-embed-ada-768 and returned 768-length vectors. When they used the alias model-embed-ada with quantization=int8 they got 384. So alias + quantization branch is the culprit.

Samir V: Affirmed. Root cause: alias resolution logic incorrectly allowed quantization to influence variant choice. The int8-optimized 384 variant was tagged to the alias for requests with quantization=int8. That's why dims changed.

Immediate mitigations:
- Ask customer to call with explicit model name (model-embed-ada-768) or omit quantization flag for now.
- We should hotfix alias map so quantization does not change dimensionality for stable aliases.
- Add server-side response headers so clients can detect dtype/dims: X-Embedding-Dims / X-Embedding-Dtype.

Tanvi K: Opening hotfix PR now to lock alias mapping and add validation: https://git.redwood/eng/embeds/PR-829 — will canary shortly.

Samir V: Longer-term: add unit tests for alias resolution, add a lint step that prevents registering variants with different dims under same alias, and update SDKs to surface dtype/dim headers and fail-fast if dims mismatch expected.

Alex P: Communicated workaround and a goodwill credit to the customer for the ingestion downtime. They've accepted the explicit-model workaround.

Maya R: Customer confirmed explicit model works and that they're unblocked. We'll keep them on the ticket until PR is live.

Tanvi K: PR merged to canary; rolling to prod in 15m. Also added server warning logs that will emit if quantization param would change dims for an alias.

Samir V: Follow-ups assigned: (1) eng-ml: reproduce with exact curl/req id (Samir) (2) eng-platform: alias guard (Tanvi) (3) docs: add quantization guidance and SDK examples (Alex)

Alex P: Marking resolved for the customer side. :white_check_mark:

Maya R: Thanks all — closing the loop on CS-9421. :heart:
